messages:
simon (Customer): Hey, after our IdP rotated certs at ~09:12 UTC users are stuck in a login loop or hitting 403 on the ACS endpoint. Most traces show Recipient/ACS mismatch or assertion errors. Any quick ideas?

maria (Support): Sorry about that — can you share a sample SAML Response (base64) or at least the HTTP headers you see at ACS? Also which IdP instance rotated?

simon (Customer): It was prod-idp via the vendor portal. Here's a captured response header excerpt: `Recipient=\"https://app.prod.example.com/sso/acs\"` while our SP expected `https://app.redwood.ai/sso/acs`. Error header: `403 saml:recipient_mismatch`. RelayState present.

deploy-bot: EVENT: IDP_CERT_ROTATION tenant=4287 signingCertId=ka87... timestamp=2024-11-28T09:12:05Z

olivia (Identity): Looking at the tenant — two quick checks: (1) did the IdP metadata change ordering of KeyDescriptor elements? our verifier picks the first signing key by default. (2) did they add an ACS alias/alternate host? If ACS host changed we fail strict recipient check.

simon (Customer): They say they only rotated certs, but vendor portal shows they also appended `app.prod.example.com` as an ACS endpoint (alias). We still send issuer `https://idp.prod.example.com` so entityID unchanged.

raj (SRE): Can you reproduce with curl against ACS so we can see raw headers? e.g.:

```
curl -i -X POST https://app.redwood.ai/sso/acs \
  -d "SAMLResponse=<base64>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded"
```

simon (Customer): Ran that, got: 

```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
x-request-id: abc123
x-saml-error: RecipientMismatch
x-saml-expected: https://app.redwood.ai/sso/acs
x-saml-actual: https://app.prod.example.com/sso/acs
```

maria (Support): That explains it — IdP is sending the alias host in the assertion. Our ACS normalizer only accepts hosts listed in SP metadata. Did they update your SP metadata to include the alias?

simon (Customer): Vendor claims they didn't touch SP metadata; only certs. But portal metadata XML shows both endpoints present now.

olivia (Identity): Two likely causes: (A) metadata propagation lag on our side — our cached IdP metadata (TTL=1h) still had old ordering/endpoints; (B) cert rotation caused vendor to re-export metadata with alias-first ordering and possibly changed KeyDescriptor order. Steps: ask customer to trigger metadata refresh from IdP or we can clear their tenant cache. Workaround: add `app.prod.example.com` to SP-allowed ACS list or configure an alias mapping in Console.

raj (SRE): I cleared the tenant metadata cache and re-fetched: `identityctl refresh-metadata --tenant 4287` — watching logs.

deploy-bot: METADATA_PULL_SUCCESS tenant=4287 source=prod-idp timestamp=2024-11-28T09:18:50Z

maria (Support): Can you try login again and paste headers if it still fails?

simon (Customer): After refresh, majority of users can log in. A handful still get 403 with `SAMLAssertion: signature verification failed`.

olivia (Identity): That one looks like a dual-key rollover issue — some assertions are signed with the old key while metadata briefly de-listed it. If the IdP disabled the old key prematurely, signatures will fail. Ask vendor to enable dual signing window or re-enable old cert for transition.

simon (Customer): Confirmed with vendor — they had disabled the old signing cert too early. They've re-enabled it for 30min and now things look green.

maria (Support): Summary/root cause: vendor rotated signing certs and simultaneously modified metadata (added ACS alias and changed KeyDescriptor ordering) while also deactivating the old signing cert. Combined with our cached metadata + strict ACS host matching this produced 403/login loops and a few signature fails. Follow-ups: (1) add tenant-level "Refresh IdP metadata" button in Console (PR #984), (2) update metadata fetcher to detect new ACS hosts and surface warnings, (3) add fallback to try alternate signing keys in verification logic. Tagging follow-ups: @olivia @raj. We'll close when you confirm stable for 24h.

simon (Customer): Thanks team :raised_hands: — will monitor and report back.
